title: Audience alignment cheatsheet: ML / backend / platform teams
body:
Purpose:
Quick, skimmable reference for SDR/solutions/growth to tailor initial outreach and demo framing for three audiences: ML engineers, backend engineers, and platform teams. Not a script; use as a lens to choose metrics, demos, and collateral.

High-level positioning (single line each):
- ML engineers: "Give me predictable, production-ready inference that keeps model outputs stable while cutting cost — so I can ship features without babysitting infrastructure."
- Backend engineers: "A high-throughput, low-latency inference endpoint that fits into existing infra and SLAs — minimal ops, strong observability, clear cost signals."
- Platform teams: "A unified runtime you can standardize on across teams and clouds — secure, policy-driven routing, and predictable economics for governance and chargeback."

TL;DR talking points to open a conversation (30–60s):
- ML: "We help you move models from prototype to production quickly: deterministic latency profiles, KV/prefix caching, and CI checks for output regressions. Typical uplift: 30–50% lower token cost via caching + batching, without noticeable quality drop."
- Backend: "We provide an API that behaves like any other service in your stack — per-route throttles, p95 latency SLOs, and transparent cost per request. Ships with SDKs and trace correlation hooks for your observability stack."
- Platform: "Standardize inference across hosted/dedicated/private deployments with the same API and rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback). Integrates with KMS, SSO, and enterprise audit logs for compliance."

Key pain signals to probe (questions):
- ML engineers: "How often does model performance drift? How painful are version rollouts? How do you detect generation regressions?"
- Backend engineers: "What percent of your endpoints have p95 > 500ms? Do you have per-route cost tracking? Any throttling or circuit-breaker needs?"
- Platform teams: "How many teams run custom models vs. shared models? Are you managing capacity commitments? Do you have requirements for VPC/air-gapped deployments?"

Core value pillars (match to persona):
- Reliability & SLOs: p50/p95 latency targets, automated fallback chains, region failover. (Backend + Platform primary)
- Cost control: batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles, cost dashboards. (ML + Platform)
- Observability & developer ergonomics: token-level breakdowns, tracing hooks, SDKs, per-route dashboards. (All)
- Compliance & isolation: VPC/private deploys, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs. (Platform primary)

Quick metrics to cite (pick 1–2 depending on audience):
- "Median latency for chat workloads: 45–80ms per token on optimized instances (depends on model)."
- "Customers see 20–40% per-token cost reduction after enabling prefix caching + model selection rules."
- "Canary rollouts reduce rollback time from hours to minutes with automated fallback policies."
- "Dedicated pools achieve linear throughput at scale for concurrent streaming workloads (examples available in docs)."

Demo playbook snippets (30–15 minute variants):
- ML 15min micro-demo: show model rollout dashboard + prompt-based evaluation (regression alert firing). Then toggle caching and show simulated token cost change.
- Backend 15min micro-demo: show API integration (SDK), trace correlation to Datadog/OTel, and per-route SLA page. Hit an endpoint to show p95 and throttling.
- Platform 30min deep: show policy-based routing (latency->region, cost->spot fallback), dedicated pool config, and single-pane audit logs + RBAC.

Objections and short rebuttals: 
- "We can just use cloud provider endpoints": "Yes — but we often see teams trade off observability and rollout controls. Redwood focuses on predictable economics and built-in rollback/canary primitives that are missing or fragmented in cloud endpoints."
- "We self-host everything": "Great — Redwood Private offers the same controls and runtime optimizations for on-prem/VPC with auditability and less engineering overhead to maintain batching/kv cache correctness."
- "Latency is the main thing, can you beat our current setup?": "We benchmark by workload and will show p50/p95 on a representative prompt; our kernel selection and batching adapt to your sequence length distribution, so wins are workload-dependent. We bring the data to you."

Collateral & content mapping (what to attach per outreach):
- ML: short eval playbook PDF, model rollout checklist, example regression alert GIF, link to developer quickstart repo.
- Backend: API quickstart snippet, SLA & latency whitepaper, trace-correlation guide.
- Platform: architecture diagram for Hosted/Dedicated/Private, compliance checklist (SOC/ISO checklist), cost allocation example for chargeback.

Language & phrasing tips (do/don't):
- Do: use concrete numbers, prefer "p95" and "tokens/sec" over vague words. Use 'canary', 'rollback', 'KV cache' — ML folks hear this.
- Don't: overpromise model quality improvements; avoid saying "we replace models" — we enable stable serving and predictable economics.

Short sample email subject lines / intros: 
- ML: "Reduce model rollouts time and cost — quick question about your inference pipeline"
- Backend: "Short: Can we help make your LLM endpoints more predictable?"
- Platform: "Standardizing inference across teams — architecture + compliance checklist attached"

Slack/LinkedIn one-liner (30–60 chars):
- ML: "Ship model features faster — fewer regressions, lower cost."
- Backend: "LLM endpoints that behave like services (p95, costs)."
- Platform: "Unified inference runtime for enterprise governance."

Conversion triggers / qualification framework (BANT-ish):
- Budget: Are you tracking inference spend monthly? threshold > $X/month -> likely upsell for Dedicated.
- Authority: Who owns infra vs model quality decisions?
- Need: Are rollouts/manual rollbacks common? Is compliance a blocker?
- Timeline: Any launches in next 3 months that require scale or privacy?

Competitor positioning cheat notes (internal reminders):
- Generic cloud endpoints: often simpler to start, but weaker in rollout controls, cost telemetry at token level. Use customer stories where we avoided an outage via fallback.
- Open-source self-hosted stacks: good control but heavy maintenance burden (kernel/quantization ops, batching correctness). Sell Private as "managed runtime, customer-controlled infra".

Open questions / To do before next iteration: 
- Add 3 anonymized metric-backed customer snippets (ml, backend, platform) — Diego to pull from CS.
- Validate the latency numbers for small vs long-context chat workflows — engineering to provide two canonical benchmark runs. (JIRA-1428)
- Build two 1-page sell sheets (ML playbook, Platform compliance) for SDR pack — Priya owns.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could add a 1-minute explainer video that shows rollout + cost dashboard side-by-side — high impact for platform execs.
- Consider templated prompts for each demo that highlight failure modes and how Redwood's fallback works.
- Keep this doc lean; create persona-specific one-pagers in /go-to-market/collateral.

End.
